name: Beryllium
occurrence: Found in beryl and emerald (beryllium aluminium silicates); rare in Earth's crust.
safetyNotes: Beryllium dust and compounds are highly toxic if inhaled and can cause chronic lung disease (berylliosis) — handled only with strict industrial controls.
notableCharacteristics: Transparent to X-rays, which is why it's used as the window material in X-ray tubes.
ncertRelevance: small size and high polarizing power effects
whyHere: Its very small +2 ion has unusually high charge density for Group 2, which is exactly what drives its diagonal relationship with aluminium rather than typical alkaline-earth behaviour.
didYouKnow: Emeralds and aquamarines are both beryllium minerals — the difference in colour comes from trace chromium versus iron impurities.
genZNote: Small, stiff, and secretly the reason your emerald exists. Also the reason X-rays can see through windows.
